breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE

phases.label: HOLD

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for a clean inbox or a perfect TNF preview to start. Fierce calm is Thursday composure when the week’s noise wants the first hour: charge first, body second, security skim when ready, Vegas and savings only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Competitors may still be refreshing injury wires or model filings; he arrives prepared for the gate. When pressure rises, he slows the breath, names the next action, and outlasts the noise. Today is not about proving anything on the scoreboard. It is about banking competitive calm so Friday’s departure window and the rest of the board have a clean operator behind them. Fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Thursday: run this after Morning Charge — box breathing first, then the body. Partly sunny outside; tempo inside before TNF and the departure gate. Then news and the day.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time. Optional: Front Clips / Back Clips if you want a second RipStick move.

Gnostic travelers warned that a journey begins the morning before the road. Guard the breath and the body first; then the coverage check and the bag. An unguarded departure leaks power into worry.
Esoteric athletes lit one lamp before reading the board. Morning Charge is that lamp. Inbox filings and injury wires are the board — useful only after the room is already lit.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.body: “Commit your work to the Lord, and your plans will be established.” (Proverbs 16:3) Solomon’s counsel for a Thursday morning is order before motion — entrust the work, then walk the plan. Morning Charge and the 3-minute opener are the committed work; a clean security skim is the next established step; Vegas coverage and savings transfers are plans that only hold after the work is already offered. Classical lore cast Solomon as one who ordered the house before the caravan left. Order the Thursday the same way, so Friday’s gate meets a settled operator — not a scrambling one.
grimoire.practice: Finish Opening Bell and the 3-minute opener before any security skim, TNF preview, or travel admin. Commit first; move second.

techDemo.title: Tech Demo
techDemo.kicker: Fast learn · from your X bookmarks
techDemo.pick: Build a full app with Claude in 26 live minutes
techDemo.author: @AnatoliKopadze

image.alt: Newsprint diagram — 26-Minute Claude App Build: Scope → Prompt → Ship

lesson.oneLiner: A Google Cloud engineer shipped a full app on stage with Claude in 26 minutes — outcome first, model second, no $500 course required.
beats: Frame: one engineer, one model, one clear goal — no team, no long setup.
Scope ruthlessly: name the app and cut everything that won’t fit a live clock.
Let Claude fill scaffold + UI + core logic while you steer the outcome.
Iterate in public: the demo has to work before the timer ends.
Same pattern as Dom’s desks: charge once → define the outcome → hand the middle to the tool.
lesson.takeaway: Under a minute: pick one tiny shippable app, set a hard timer, and make Claude the pair-programmer — not the boss.
